passages.title: Love and truth shape the limits of welcome during a teaching conflict
passages.summary: The elder writes to the chosen lady and her children. He rejoices that some of her children walk in truth. He asks that they love one another, as commanded from the beginning. Love means walking by God’s commandments. Many deceivers deny that Jesus Christ came in the flesh. Whoever goes beyond Christ’s teaching does not have God. They should not receive such a teacher into the house. The elder hopes to come and speak face to face.
passages.uncertainty: Second John names no place, so the map shows none.

lds.text: The selected Church lesson uses this warning to discuss remaining in Christ's teaching. How does walking in received teaching connect love with responsible welcome?

contextNote.title: Love and truth shape the limits of welcome during a teaching conflict
contextNote.text: Verse 5 asks for love and says the command is not new. Verse 6 defines the word: love is walking by his commandments. The command is the one heard from the beginning. That definition prepares for verse 7, where deceivers bring a different teaching. Verse 10 then limits welcome. A house should not receive one who does not bring Christ’s teaching.
